The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of the changes I made to fix ordering by deeply-nested relation paths (2+ hops) including many-to-many relations:

## Changes

### 1. `query-engine/query-structure/src/order_by.rs`
Added two methods on `OrderByToManyAggregation`:
- **`intermediary_hops(&self) -> &[OrderByHop]`** — returns all hops except the final aggregation hop (the JOIN chain leading up to the aggregated model).
- **`aggregation_hop(&self) -> &OrderByHop`** — returns the last hop, on which the aggregation (e.g. `_count`) is performed.

### 2. `query-engine/connectors/sql-query-connector/src/join_utils.rs`
Added **`compute_m2m_join`**, which traverses a many-to-many relation as an order-by hop. Unlike a one-to-many hop (a single JOIN), an m2m hop emits **two** JOINs — one onto the implicit join table and one onto the related model table — with the related-model alias exposed for subsequent hops.

### 3. `query-engine/connectors/sql-query-connector/src/ordering.rs`
- Rewrote `compute_joins_aggregation` to use `intermediary_hops()` for the intermediate JOIN chain and `aggregation_hop()` for the final aggregation JOIN.
- Introduced `compute_hop_joins`, which dispatches each hop to `compute_one2m_join` (one join) or `compute_m2m_join` (two joins) based on whether the relation is m2m — so mixed one-to-many / many-to-many chains traverse correctly.
- Refactored both `compute_joins_aggregation` and `compute_joins_scalar` to track a running `previous_alias` rather than index-based lookup, so multi-join hops chain correctly. Join-prefix counters remain identical to before for the pure one-to-one/one-to-many cases, so existing SQL is byte-for-byte unchanged.
